title: Make ALL board models agentic via opencode (re-investigate commandcode + GLM custom provider)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§7, ref #75).

## What
Make every board model run **agentically** (tool-using) via opencode, not just the codex seat. Re-investigate:
- **commandcode** as the agentic runner path.
- A **GLM custom provider** wired into opencode.

## Why
Today only the codex seat is agentic (GPT-5.5). A review board where every seat can actually run tools/read the repo gives materially better findings than chat-only seats.

## Acceptance
- Board models route through opencode agentically where the provider supports it.
- commandcode + GLM custom provider investigated and either wired or rejected with a reason.
- `review` board output reflects agentic capability per seat (capability-tagged).

title: spec-web: draft autosave race — server-side ordering token/tombstone
body:
Follow-up from #29 review (codex P2).

The client mitigates the in-flight-autosave-resurrection race with an abortable fetch + a TRAILING `clearDraftOnServer` after create/edit. But a client-side abort cannot recall a request already sent: if a non-empty autosave POST reaches the server's per-slot lock AFTER the clear delete (lock-acquisition order ≠ send order), it re-creates the draft and a reload can resurrect stale composer text.

**Proper fix:** server-side ordering — stamp each `/api/drafts/<slot>` write with a monotonic token (client send-sequence or server receive-time) and have the store REJECT a write older than the slot's last applied token (a tombstone on clear). Then a late autosave can't overwrite a newer clear regardless of lock-acquisition order. Replaces the client's best-effort ordering assumption.

**Severity:** P2, low-probability timing edge; consequence is a recoverable stale draft (not data loss). The common case is already handled. Tracked separately from #29 to avoid destabilizing the 9-round-reviewed phase-2 diff.

title: Harden _ensure_opencode_readonly_agent: validate/refuse a pre-existing permissive global read-only-reviewer agent
body:
Follow-up from review-cli#24 (agentic default board) — codex review finding.

## Problem
`reviewlib/backends.py` `_ensure_opencode_readonly_agent` trusts an EXISTING global `~/.config/opencode/agents/read-only-reviewer.md` without validating its permissions. Now that the DEFAULT board's Kimi/GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek seats run agentically through opencode (review-cli#24), `review_opencode` runs on every default `review`. If that global agent file was previously created (by the user or another tool) with `bash`/`edit`/`write` ALLOWED, the default board would run `opencode --dir <repo>` with write/tool access — violating the read-only promise.

This is PRE-EXISTING (it applied to any `oc:` usage before #24), but #24 makes it the default path, raising exposure.

## Fix
Validate the existing `read-only-reviewer` agent's permissions before reusing it; if it is not the expected deny-all definition, either overwrite it or refuse agentic mode (fall back to the diff-only path) with a clear message. Add a test with a pre-existing permissive agent definition.

## Source
codex (gpt-5.5, xhigh) pre-commit review of the #24 PR.

title: review-qa Phase 1: mode skeleton + no-suites gate
body:
## What

Phase 1 (Increment 1) of the `review qa` "agent-as-tester" mode, per `docs/specs/review-qa.md` — the smallest independently-shippable, verifiable slice. NO executor, NO LLM-judge, NO env-harness yet (those are Phase 2+).

This slice ships:
- A new `reviewlib/modes/qa.py` exposing `MODE = ModeSpec(name="qa", subcommand="qa", diff_policy="none", aliases=("test",), ...)`, registered in `reviewlib/modes/registry.py` (one import + one entry).
- `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES` exit code in `reviewlib/cli.py` next to the existing `EXIT_*` constants.
- A minimal suite-discovery stub (`resolve_suites`) looking in a conventional dir (`docs/tests/suites/*.md`, relative to the SUT) for prose `## Case:` markdown suites.
- The **no-suites gate**: when `qa` runs but no authored suites/cases resolve, FAIL with a 3-part WHAT/WHY/HOW message (mirroring `cli._fail_not_a_repo`) and exit `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES`. "A green qa run with zero authored cases is a lie." The gate runs BEFORE any agent/docker/browser.
- Handler stops after the gate (Phase 1 has no launcher) with a clear "not yet implemented: executor (Phase 2)" notice when suites DO resolve.

## Why

`review qa` makes an agent act as a tester. Without authored test cases there is nothing to exercise and nothing to verify — a green run would be a lie. The mandatory no-suites gate is the load-bearing contract of the whole mode, and it is independently shippable + testable without the (large, security-sensitive) write/exec executor.

## Acceptance criteria

- `review qa` and `review test` (alias) resolve to the qa mode via the registry (`get_mode`).
- `review qa --help` works.
- With no suites authored for the target, the run exits `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES` (5 unless taken) and prints a 3-part WHAT/WHY/HOW message.
- A non-empty suite file with `## Case:` blocks parses to a non-zero case count (Phase 1: discovery/parse only; no execution).
- Tests cover: (a) the qa mode + its `test` alias resolve via the registry; (b) the no-suites gate fires and exits `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES` with the 3-part message.
- Full review-cli test suite green; ruff clean.

Spec: `docs/specs/review-qa.md` (§4 NO-SUITES gate, §6 exit codes, "Phased implementation plan" → Increment 1).

title: review-qa Phase 2: write/exec agentic executor + judge + 2-fixture DoD
body:
## What

Phase 2 / Increment 2 of `review qa` (`docs/specs/review-qa.md`, "Phased implementation plan"): the **write/exec AGENTIC EXECUTOR** — the piece that actually drives a System-Under-Test (SUT) against authored prose `## Case:` suites and classifies PASS/FAIL with evidence. Replaces the Phase-1 `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED=70` scaffold with the real executor path.

Phase 1 (PR #55, on main) shipped the mode skeleton + no-suites gate + `EXIT_QA_NO_SUITES=6`.

## Decided design (multi-model brainstorm, spec §11 — encoded, not re-opened)

- **Tester backend:** claude by DEFAULT; codex opt-in via `REVIEW_QA_TESTER=codex` (`codex exec -s workspace-write --full-auto`). opencode OUT of v1.
- qa does **NOT** ride `run_panel`/the board and must NOT call `_ensure_opencode_readonly_agent`. A new thin `reviewlib/qa/executor.py` spawns ONE write/exec-capable backend (claude: a write/exec profile, NOT the read-only `--disallowedTools` spawn). A comment by `_READONLY_AGENT_DENIED_PERMISSIONS` records qa as the deliberate write/exec exception.
- **Isolation:** run the tester in an isolated `git worktree add` of the SUT (default); `--in-place` escape hatch.
- **Single-seat** (handler collapses `ctx.models` to one seat; no cli.py model-resolution surgery).
- **Output: report-only, NO gating** — findings + proof; a found bug never fails the build (exit 0 with findings printed). Only infra failures exit non-zero. `--strict` flips a FAIL verdict to exit 10.
- **Cost cap (mandatory):** `--max-cases 1` DEFAULT, serial execution, per-run timeout, token + wall-time accounting in the report. qa gets a LONG timeout, not the short `PANEL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.
- **Suite format:** Markdown-prose `## Case:` blocks (Phase 1 discovery). The tester reads the prose case, drives the SUT, and self-judges PASS/FAIL with evidence in a machine-parsed `## QA RESULTS` tail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `reviewlib/qa/{__init__,executor,suites}.py`: write/exec launcher (claude default, codex alternate), isolated worktree by default + `--in-place`, single-seat, streaming to `--report`, cleanup on exit/signal.
- [ ] `_build_tester_prompt` + `## QA RESULTS` tail parser → verdict→exit mapping (PASS=0, FAIL=1, FAIL+`--strict`=10, BLOCKED=8, no-VERDICT=1).
- [ ] Replace `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED=70` with the real executor path; add `EXIT_QA_SUT_BOOT_FAILED`.
- [ ] Timeout carve-out so qa gets a long default, not `PANEL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`.
- [ ] Comment by `_READONLY_AGENT_DENIED_PERMISSIONS` recording the qa write/exec exception.
- [ ] **DoD:** two committed fixtures — a tiny SUT with a KNOWN BUG (must-FAIL case) and a known-GOOD variant (must-PASS case) + their prose `## Case:` suites. A test runs the executor against both and asserts the buggy one classifies FAIL (with evidence) and the good one PASS. Cost-capped (1 case, tiny fixture, short timeout).
- [ ] Live-backend DoD test gated behind `REVIEW_QA_LIVE=1`; a deterministic **mocked-tester** unit test exercises the executor/judge plumbing in normal CI.
- [ ] Full suite green (`python tests/smoke.py`), ruff clean, review-gate `[ok]`.

## Security

First WRITE/EXEC agent in review-cli. Isolation must be real: isolated worktree by default, never the user's checkout unless `--in-place`. `--full-auto` + `--in-place` against a repo with unpushed changes is refused.

Closes via the Phase-2 PR.

comments.body:
## Progress

Branch `feat/review-qa-executor` (worktree). Implementation complete; in final review-gate pass.

**Done:**
- `reviewlib/qa/{__init__,executor,suites}.py` — write/exec launcher (claude default / codex via `REVIEW_QA_TESTER`), isolated `git worktree` by default + `--in-place`, single-seat, streaming, cleanup on every exit/signal path (incl. mid-run exception + `worktree prune` on failed remove).
- `_build_tester_prompt` (§8) + `## QA RESULTS` parser → verdict→exit mapping (PASS=0, FAIL=0 report-only / 10 under `--strict`, BLOCKED=8, UNKNOWN=1). Hardened: PASS requires `cases_run>=1`; the unfilled `VERDICT: PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED` placeholder → UNKNOWN; first-real-verdict selection.
- Replaced `EXIT_QA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED=70` scaffold with the real executor; added `EXIT_QA_SUT_BOOT_FAILED=8` (+ reserved `NO_ENV=7`/`ENV_UNHEALTHY=9`).
- Timeout carve-out: qa gets `QA_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT=2700s`, not the 240s panel default.
- Comment by `_READONLY_AGENT_DENIED_PERMISSIONS` recording the deliberate write/exec exception.
- `--kind auto` stdlib detection (ext/web/bot/backend).

**Security (first un-caged agent):**
- Default isolation = throwaway `git worktree` of the SUT; prompt built at the ACTUAL run cwd (the worktree), never the user's checkout. Default report written OUTSIDE the SUT tree (review-cli log dir) so a clean checkout stays clean.
- `--in-place` over a dirty git tree refused for BOTH seats (claude `bypassPermissions` and codex `--full-auto`); non-git in-place allowed (nothing to dirty).
- README states plainly: the worktree fences SUT *mutations*, NOT reads/exfiltration — not an OS sandbox.

**DoD (2 fixtures under `tests/fixtures/qa/`):** tiny shell SUT with a known off-by-one bug (`add 2 2 → 5`, must-FAIL) + a known-good variant (`→ 4`, must-PASS), each with a prose `## Case:` suite.
- **Mocked-tester DoD** (CI, deterministic, no backend): buggy → FAIL+finding, good → PASS. Runs in `python tests/smoke.py`.
- **Live-backend DoD** gated on `REVIEW_QA_LIVE=1` (skipped in CI). Verified live with the codex seat: buggy fixture's authored case FAILS with cited evidence (`stdout 5 vs expected 4`), good fixture's authored case PASSES.

`python tests/smoke.py` green, ruff clean, three review-gate rounds [ok] (findings addressed each round).

title: Add GLM 5.2 via commandcode as a read-only review board seat, priority directly under Opus
body:
## Context

The CTO wants GLM 5.2 (Zhipu GLM) added as a review backend, placed in the board priority order **immediately after `claude:claude-opus-4-8`** (so the pool tries Opus first, then GLM 5.2).

## Current state (already wired)
- GLM 5.2 already exists in `DEFAULT_BOARD` at **priority 5** as `oc:zai/glm-5.2` (agentic via opencode's `zai` provider), routing through the user's z.ai Coding-Plan subscription.
- A diff-only `zai:glm-5.2` REST backend (`review_zai`) and `-m glm`/`glm52` aliases also exist.
- `commandcode` in review-cli is an **OpenAI-compatible HTTP Provider API gateway** (`https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1`), keyed by `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` — **NOT a CLI/binary**. (`COMMANDCODE_SUPPORTED_MODES = ("api",)` — there is no commandcode CLI.)

## What's missing
The CTO specifically asked for GLM 5.2 **via commandcode**, and placed **right under Opus**. Verified the commandcode gateway serves `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (live chat-completion test returns content, finish_reason=stop). So:

1. Add a GLM-5.2-via-commandcode board seat at **priority 3** (directly under Opus at priority 2), pushing Codex/Kimi/etc. down one.
2. Wire its model id against the commandcode gateway catalog: `commandcode:zai-org/GLM-5.2` (agentic form `oc:commandcode/zai-org/GLM-5.2` if opencode's commandcode provider serves it, else the diff-only keyed-HTTP `commandcode:zai-org/GLM-5.2` REST seat).
3. Read-only by construction (REST backends POST only the diff; agentic commandcode-via-opencode runs read-only in `-C`). No write/exec.
4. Degrade gracefully when COMMANDCODE_API_KEY / commandcode is absent (like other absent backends).

## Acceptance
- Board seat registers and sits at priority 3, directly under Opus.
- Availability degrades gracefully when commandcode key is absent.
- Spawn is read-only.
- `python tests/smoke.py` green, ruff clean.

title: review qa: --visual is built (paid) by cli.py then dropped — thread it or reject it pre-pipeline
body:
## Deferred from review-qa Phase 2 (#56)

A codex review of the Phase-2 executor flagged: `review qa --visual shot.png` runs the shared visual companion pipeline (a paid vision call, built in `cli.py` for every mode at ~`cli.py:1818`) and then the qa handler never reads `ctx.visual_ctx` / never calls `ctx.with_visual()` — so the visual context is silently dropped.

A handler-level reject is INEFFECTIVE: `cli.py` fully resolves/handles `--visual` (cvGate + companion build) BEFORE dispatching to the qa handler, so a guard in the handler never fires (verified: `review qa --visual <png> --no-ai` returns from the visual path, not the handler).

## Fix options
1. **Thread it in:** fold `ctx.with_visual()` / `ctx.visual_ctx` into `build_tester_prompt` so a screenshot becomes grounding context for the tester (e.g. "here's the expected UI").
2. **Reject pre-pipeline:** skip the visual companion build for `mode.name == "qa"` in `cli.py` (a small, mode-aware gate before the paid fan-out) and print a "qa doesn't use --visual" usage error.

Option 2 is the smaller, safer v1 fix (qa produces its OWN visual proof by driving the SUT). Either way, add a CLI test.

Low priority — `--visual` + qa is an uncommon combination; tracked so it isn't lost.

comments.body: Fixed in the Phase-2 PR: qa now rejects --visual in cli.py BEFORE the vision pipeline runs (exit 2, 'not supported'), with a test. Codex re-raised it during review so I addressed it inline rather than deferring.

title: review qa: forward -m model suffix to the tester + clean up ephemeral-worktree trust entries
body:
## Deferred from review-qa Phase 2 (#56)

Two lower-impact hardening items a codex review flagged on the Phase-2 executor; both are P2 and deferred to keep the Phase-2 PR focused.

### 1. `-m claude:<model>` / `-m codex:<model>` suffix is dropped
`resolved_tester_backend` reduces `-m claude:claude-opus-4-8` to just `claude`, and `_spawn_claude_writeexec` / `_spawn_codex_writeexec` never pass a `--model` flag — so a requested model suffix is silently ignored (the backend's own default model runs). Either forward the suffix to the spawn (`claude-p --model <m>` / `codex -m <m>`) or reject a suffixed qa tester with a clear message.

### 2. Ephemeral-worktree trust entries accumulate in `~/.claude.json`
`_spawn_claude_writeexec` calls `_ensure_workspace_trusted(<temp worktree>)` (needed — a fresh worktree is untrusted and claude's headless gate blocks on it), but `IsolatedSut.__exit__` removes only the worktree dir, not the persisted trust entry. Over many default qa runs, `~/.claude.json` accumulates trusted `/tmp/review-qa-wt-*` paths that no longer exist. Clean up the trust entry after the claude run (or use a non-persistent trust mechanism for ephemeral worktrees).

Neither blocks normal use; tracked so they aren't lost.

title: review qa: --kind auto bot-detection misses Python projects; help config omits qa
body:
## Deferred from review-qa Phase 2 (#56)

Two low-impact polish items a codex review flagged; deferred to keep the Phase-2 PR focused.

### 1. `--kind auto` bot detection only reads package.json
`_looks_like_bot()` inspects `package.json` deps (`telegraf`/`grammy`/`python-telegram-bot`/`aiogram`), but a normal **Python** bot project uses `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml`, so it falls back to `backend` and gets the wrong runbook. Either parse Python dependency files for the python bot markers, or drop the python markers from the detector. Add a Python-bot fixture test. (Low impact: the agent is the real detector; `auto` only seeds the runbook, and the user can pass `--kind bot` explicitly.)

### 2. `review help config` omits qa from the model-selection cascade
The deep `review help config` topic still describes `models:` / `DEFAULT_MODELS` without noting that **qa ignores them** and uses `REVIEW_QA_TESTER` / a bare `-m codex|claude`. The per-mode `--help` was updated; the deep topic should get a qa row too, with a test.

Neither blocks normal use; tracked so they aren't lost.

title: review-qa Phase 3: SUT env bring-up — detect/reuse/health-gate/guaranteed-teardown
body:
## What

Phase 3 of \`review qa\`: the SUT ENVIRONMENT bring-up layer (\`reviewlib/qa/env.py\`) that stands up the System-Under-Test before the Phase-2 executor drives it.

Lifecycle (spec docs/specs/review-qa.md §7.2):
1. **stage-detect** — is the SUT already reachable at a configured health endpoint/command?
2. **reuse-if-reachable** — NEVER tear down what we didn't bring up (symmetric ownership).
3. else **bring-up** via (a) a \`qa/setup.sh\` / \`<sut>/.review-qa/setup.sh\` hook (lightweight default), or (b) \`docker compose -p <namespaced> up -d --wait\` (heavier, reuses the \`-p\` isolation pattern).
4. **health-gate** — poll the configured health check; fail \`EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY\` if it never comes up.
5. hand the running env to the Phase-2 executor.
6. **guaranteed teardown** — only of what THIS run brought up; reused envs are left running.

## Exit codes (already reserved in cli.py; +1-shifted from the spec because brainstorm took 5)
- \`EXIT_QA_NO_ENV = 7\` — no stage AND no bring-up config for a backend/bot SUT.
- \`EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY = 9\` — bring-up succeeded but the health gate timed out (infra, NOT a bug).
- (\`EXIT_QA_SUT_BOOT_FAILED = 8\` is Phase 2's.)

## Teardown safety (the adversarial must-fix, spec lines 592/601)
backstop.py only SIGKILLs registered subprocess GROUPS; \`docker compose up -d\` daemonizes into the Docker daemon and is in no child group of review — so SIGKILL leaves every container running. Phase 3 ships a REAL atexit/signal teardown hook keyed by the \`-p\` project name, independent of subprocess reaping. Teardown NEVER kills a reused stage (ownership rule) and only ever targets the namespaced \`-p\` project we created.

## Definition of done
- (a) a reachable stage env is REUSED and NOT torn down;
- (b) a \`qa/setup.sh\`-hook env is brought up, health-gated, handed off, and torn down on exit;
- (c) an env that never becomes healthy fails \`EXIT_QA_ENV_UNHEALTHY\` with teardown still run;
- (d) teardown is guaranteed even when the executor throws/times out.
- Docker-dependent tests gated behind \`REVIEW_QA_DOCKER=1\`; deterministic hook/mocked tests for normal CI.

title: board resilience under concurrent load: per-seat timeout + slow-reserve-seat deprioritize + memory-aware concurrency cap
body:
## Problem (observed live)

When ~6 subagents each run \`review diff --staged --pool 1 -m claude:claude-opus-4-8\` concurrently (plus a \`review quorum --pool 3\`), reviews became very slow and some seats died mid-review ("opus died mid-review, single startup line, exit 1" -> agents fell back to codex).

Earlier finding (rig-w4): \`review\` at \`--pool 4\` OOM-kills under swarm load, and the \`oc:zai/glm-5.2\` reserve seat is pathologically slow.

So under real concurrent load the board is fragile:
- **memory pressure** from too many concurrent heavy model subprocesses (each board seat spawns a codex/claude/opencode CLI child; \`run_panel\` uses \`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs))\` with NO global cap on concurrent children);
- a **pathologically-slow reserve seat** (\`oc:zai/glm-5.2\`, priority 6) that, when promoted, can stall the pool's path to a verdict.

## Root cause (code)

- \`reviewlib/panel.py\` \`run_panel\` / \`run_panel_with_retry\`: \`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs))\` -> unbounded concurrent model subprocesses per invocation; nothing caps the total across a high \`--pool\`.
- No process-wide semaphore around \`subprocess.Popen\` in \`reviewlib/process.py:_run_streamed\`.
- \`oc:zai/glm-5.2\` sits at priority 6 (first agentic reserve after Kimi at #5) — a slow seat on the reserve critical path.

## Fix (combination)

1. **Memory-aware concurrency cap**: a process-wide semaphore around the heavy model subprocess spawn (\`_run_streamed\`), bounding concurrent children regardless of \`--pool\`. Default cap, overridable via \`\$REVIEW_MAX_CONCURRENCY\`.
2. **Per-seat hard timeout** already enforced by \`_run_streamed\` (proc.wait(timeout) -> SIGKILL group, rc 124); verify a slow/hung seat is dropped after the timeout and the board returns with the seats that answered. Harden if not.
3. **Deprioritize the known-slow \`oc:zai/glm-5.2\` reserve seat** so it is not on the critical path by default (still available as the lowest agentic reserve, but not blocking a fast verdict).
4. **Resilience**: a seat that dies mid-review (exit 1 / empty) is treated as a non-answer and the board proceeds with the rest rather than failing the whole review (verify; harden).

Keep the single-seat \`--pool 1 -m claude:claude-opus-4-8\` gate path (everyone's pre-commit gate) working + fast.

## Acceptance

- A slow/hanging seat is dropped after the timeout (board still returns).
- A dying seat is a non-answer, not a board failure.
- The concurrency cap holds (no more than N concurrent heavy children per process).
- The single-seat gate path is unaffected.
- Full suite green; ruff clean.

title: review qa: bot Tier-1 hermetic harness (fake Telegram + inject/capture driver)
body:
## What

The per-SUT-TYPE **bot Tier-1 hermetic harness** for \`review qa\` (Increment 5 of the phased plan in \`docs/specs/review-qa.md\` §7.3 / §10). review-qa is shipped through Phase 3 (the write/exec executor #62 + the SUT env bring-up layer #64). What's deferred is the per-kind harnesses: web (Playwright), VS Code ext, and BOT. This issue is the BOT harness, **Tier-1 (hermetic)** — the bot driven against a fake Telegram Bot API, deterministic, no live token/network.

## Why

Today \`review qa --kind bot\` only injects a prose RUNBOOK into the tester prompt and tells the agent to "spin up a mock Bot-API server" by hand. There is no deterministic, reusable mechanism to:
- bring a bot-under-test up pointed at a HERMETIC fake Telegram (no real token, no network),
- inject synthetic inbound \`getUpdates\` updates ("a human typed this"),
- capture the bot's outbound \`sendMessage\` calls,
- classify a case PASS/FAIL with evidence.

A green \`--kind bot\` run today proves nothing — the agent has no fake-Telegram to drive. Spec §7.3 Tier 1: a local fake Bot-API server the bot polls via \`TG_API_BASE\` (\`tg-ctl\` already honors it); the harness POSTs synthetic updates and asserts captured sends.

## Scope (Tier 1 only)

- **Hermetic fake Telegram Bot API server** (stdlib HTTP): accepts \`getUpdates\` (returns queued injected updates), \`sendMessage\`/\`sendPhoto\`/\`answerCallbackQuery\`/etc (captures + 200s), \`getMe\`/\`deleteWebhook\`/etc (benign stubs). In-process inject + capture API for the deterministic driver.
- **A bot driver** that resolves the bot's run command from \`docs/tests/qa.yaml\` (\`sut.bot\`), boots it with \`TG_API_BASE\` pointed at the fake, runs the prose \`## Case:\` suite (send update -> expect outbound), classifies, **guaranteed teardown** (reuse the Phase-3 env backstop + ownership rules).
- **A real fixture**: a tiny example bot (good + buggy variant), a prose suite ("/start -> welcome message"), driven through the hermetic harness, proving must-pass (good bot -> PASS) + must-fail (buggy bot -> FAIL with a finding). Mirrors the Phase-2 DoD fixture pattern.

## Out of scope (deferred, tracked separately)

- **Tier 2** (real MTProto/Telethon user account + agent-browser Telegram Web, \`requires_live_telegram\`) — needs provisioned test creds + test DC. Deferred per spec §7.3 / open decision #7.
- Other bot frameworks beyond the generic Bot-API-polling shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- The fake-Telegram server brings up, accepts \`getUpdates\`, returns injected updates, captures outbound \`sendMessage\`; deterministic, no network.
- A positive capability probe at setup (call \`sendMessage\` against the fake, assert it is captured) so "zero sends" can't false-pass an un-patched/silent bot (spec footgun).
- Must-pass fixture (good bot) -> PASS; must-fail (buggy bot) -> FAIL with a finding.
- Teardown guaranteed on every exit path (normal + signal/atexit), only of what this run owns.
- Full \`python tests/smoke.py\` green; ruff clean; deterministic so it runs in normal CI.

## Why

review-qa is shipped through Phase 3 (executor + SUT env) and the BOT Tier-1 harness. The remaining harnesses are WEB (Playwright) and VS Code ext. Tier-1 web = deterministic: bring the web app up, wait for it to be reachable, drive it with a headless browser, assert DOM/behavior — no flaky network, no un-caged agent. This is the per-kind analogue of the bot deterministic path: "goto/click/fill -> expect DOM" is a mechanical assertion that needs no write/exec agent.

## Scope (this issue)

- A web SUT harness (`reviewlib/qa/web_harness.py`): bring the web app up (`sut.web.command` dev-server / setup), health-gate it reachable, then drive it with Playwright (headless Chromium).
- A deterministic driver (`reviewlib/qa/web_driver.py`): parse the prose `## Case:` grammar (`Goto:` / `Click:` / `Fill:` / `Expect-text:` / `Expect-url:` / `Expect-no:`) into Playwright actions + assertions, classify PASS/FAIL with evidence (failing selector/text, optional screenshot), emit the same `## QA RESULTS` contract the executor parser reads.

- Playwright gated behind `REVIEW_QA_PLAYWRIGHT=1` + skip-with-clear-message when the browser isn't installed; the PURE logic (grammar parser -> action mapping, QA RESULTS emission) is unit-tested deterministically WITHOUT a browser (mock page object), so it gates in normal CI.
- A real fixture: a tiny static web app + a prose suite, with a must-pass (good app) and a must-fail (buggy app — wrong text) variant proving PASS and FAIL+finding — mirroring the bot-good / bot-buggy DoD.

## Out of scope (deferred, tracked separately)

- VS Code ext harness.

title: review diff/just-ask --staged -C <repo> mis-resolves the diff to the process cwd's repo, not the -C repo
body:
## What is wrong

`review diff --staged -C <repoB>` (and `review just-ask --staged -C <repoB>`) computes the git diff from the WRONG repository when invoked from a different cwd. Run from inside worktree A, `review diff --staged -C /path/to/B` reviews A's staged diff (or whatever repo encloses the process cwd) instead of B's staged diff.

This is the EXACT command every review-gate uses: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1 -C <worktree>`. A mis-resolved diff means the gate has been reviewing the WRONG (or empty) diff — a likely major cause of the 'review returns nothing / banner-only' degradation agents kept hitting (mis-attributed to the weekly cap).

## Evidence (to be captured RED-first)

A test that runs the diff pipeline with `-C repoB` from process-cwd repoA and asserts the diff text passed to the backend is repoB's staged content, not repoA's. Covers both the `diff` review mode and `just-ask --staged`.

## Root cause (suspected)

The `git diff [--cached]` invocation does not run anchored to the resolved `-C` repo in every path — it picks up the process cwd or mis-resolves to an unrelated enclosing worktree.

## Fix

Make the staged-diff and unstaged-diff computation ALWAYS run against the resolved `-C` repo root — `git -C <resolved_repo_root> diff [--cached]` — for the diff review, just-ask --staged, AND the marker/stamp diff (keep the stamp+tool aligned, per #18). Resolve the repo root from `-C` (or its default), never the process cwd.

## Acceptance criteria

- From cwd A, `review diff --staged -C B` reviews B's staged diff, not A's.
- Same for `review just-ask --staged -C B`.
- All diff-acquisition paths (review + just-ask --staged + stamp/marker) use one identical `-C`-anchored git invocation.
- RED-first repro test passes; full smoke green; ruff clean.

body:

Completes the bot/web/ext trio.

## Why (consequence of not fixing)

review-qa Phase 3 + bot + web shipped, but VS Code extensions — the CTO's primary SUT shape (hyperide) — have NO deterministic harness. Today a `--kind ext` run falls through to the un-caged executor with only a prose runbook; there is no reproducible, no-model, deterministic "run this command -> expect this notification/editor-text/webview" path the way bot/web have. Without it the trio is incomplete and ext SUTs can't be tested in normal CI.

## Evidence / template (verified)

- `reviewlib/qa/web_harness.py` + `web_driver.py` — the closest template (heavy browser dep gated behind `REVIEW_QA_PLAYWRIGHT=1`, a `PageDriver` protocol seam keeping the parser/QA-RESULTS emission browser-free + unit-testable, a 2-fixture good->PASS / buggy->FAIL DoD).

The ext harness REUSES/adapts this pattern via a TS runner, not reinvents it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ext_harness.py` (the heavy VS Code launch, gated behind `REVIEW_QA_VSCODE=1`, skip-with-clear-message when VS Code/node not available) + `ext_driver.py` (the `## Case:` grammar -> VS Code automation parser + classifier + `## QA RESULTS` emitter), decoupled behind an `ExtDriver` protocol so the PURE logic is unit-testable with NO VS Code launch.

title: review-qa ext harness: follow-up hardening (live-runner robustness + glue/timeout test coverage)
body:
Follow-ups from the #74 (ext Tier-1 harness) review — all LOW priority, non-blocking notes the claude review-gate seat surfaced. Tracked so they aren't dropped.

## Live-runner robustness (only affects the gated REVIEW_QA_VSCODE=1 live leg, never the deterministic CI path)
- **Command-palette-by-id is brittle.** `ext_runner.mts` drives commands via `F1` + typing the command ID into the palette, but the palette matches by TITLE, not id, so it works only for commands whose title matches. The robust fix is to register a tiny helper command in the launched VS Code that calls `commands.executeCommand(id)` directly (as the docstring promises), or to drive executeCommand over a VS Code automation API. Today the live leg is best-effort.
- **`select` + buffered `text=True` readline in `ShellRunnerAutomation._read_reply`.** A partial line without a trailing `\n`, or bytes already sitting in Python's text-mode buffer above the OS pipe, can make `select` miss data (false timeout) or `readline()` block past the deadline. Low risk (the runner writes one full line per request), but a latent fragility — switch to a byte-level buffered reader or a reader thread + queue.

## Isolation docstring mismatch
- **Absolute `extension_path`/`workspace` in qa.yaml silently bypass worktree isolation.** `_launch_and_drive_ext` does `(cwd / abs).resolve()` which drops `cwd` when the config path is absolute, so an absolute path escapes the isolated worktree without a warning — while the docstring says "relative to the run cwd". Either warn on an absolute path under the default (non-`--in-place`) worktree run, or document the escape explicitly.

## Test coverage gaps (the deterministic logic is well covered; these are the harness-orchestration + timeout paths)
- No test for the timeout/hang path of `_await_ready` (launch never signals ready) and `_read_reply` (runner dies mid-reply) — the comments claim the behavior, no test pins it. Add a unit test with a tiny fake runner script (a python/sh one-liner) that hangs / exits early, asserting the controlled ExtHarnessError/ExtActionError + the boot-failed exit class.
- `modes/qa.py` orchestration glue (`_run_ext_deterministic`, `_emit_ext_blocked`, `_drive_ext_in_isolation`, the dirty-tree warning, worktree-vs-`--in-place`) is covered only indirectly via `_resolve_deterministic_ext`. Add a handler-level test driving the BLOCKED path (REVIEW_QA_VSCODE off) end-to-end against the fixture, asserting the exit class + the report write.
- `ShellRunnerAutomation._read_reply`'s skip-logic (out-of-order id, non-JSON lines, runner-death) is the stated resilience logic but has no unit test — drive it against an in-memory fake stdin/stdout.

## Deferred features (out of scope for v1, parked)
- Tier-2 visual: window-screenshot diffing for rendered UI correctness.
- More command/assertion types (status bar, quick-pick, diagnostics, terminal output).
- Publish the reference `ext_runner.mts` as the standalone `vscode-playwright` package (spec §7.1) and wire `rig doctor` to verify it.

comments.body:
Second-round review notes (PR #74, after the first-round fixes landed):

- **Buffered readline above select() (latent, low risk).** `select.select([stdout],...)` polls the OS fd but `readline()` reads from Python's text-mode buffer; if the runner emits several lines in one burst, select may signal ready once while extra lines sit in the buffer until the next select wait. One full line per request makes this very low risk, but a byte-level reader (or a reader-thread + queue) would remove the edge entirely. Applies to both `_read_reply` and `_await_ready`.
- **Localized command titles (`%nls.key%`) — partially addressed.** The runner's title map now resolves `%key%` against `package.nls.json` and skips an unresolved key (falling back to the id). A fuller fix would also read locale-specific `package.nls.<locale>.json` bundles. Tracked here for completeness.

title: claude:claude-opus-4-8 review seat returns corrupted/unparseable verdict (TUI-scraper bleed via claude-p) — degrades primary review-gate
body:
## Problem

The `claude:claude-opus-4-8` seat is the PRIMARY/default review-gate seat. It frequently returns an unreadable/corrupted or empty verdict, forcing agents to fall back to gemini/codex all session. Reported symptom: "the opus seat's output was clobbered by an interactive harness fullscreen-renderer prompt bleeding into its TTY".

## Root cause

review-cli invokes the claude seat via `claude-p` (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/claude-p`), which is a **TUI-scraper**: its own docstring says it "does not invoke \`claude -p\`. It starts interactive \`claude\` under a PTY" (`pty.openpty()`) and screen-scrapes the assistant text. That scrape is lossy (wide glyphs, cursor redraws, spinner smears). When the scrape is imperfect or hits an interactive block, claude-p's own stdout — which review-cli captures verbatim — is garbled, banner-only, or empty.

review-cli's spawn (`reviewlib/process.py` `_run_streamed`) captures `claude-p` stdout over a **pipe** (good: no extra PTY on review's side), but:
1. **No ANSI/control-sequence stripping** is applied to the captured seat `stdout` before parsing/usability checks (`reviewlib/panel.py` `format_result`/`result_is_usable`). A stray escape sequence corrupts the rendered `## claude:claude-opus-4-8 [ok]` verdict. The existing `_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE` in `reviewlib/cli.py` is applied ONLY to the `-o` output file, not to the verdict pipeline.
2. The claude backend doesn't force a fully non-interactive child environment (`TERM=dumb`, stdin from a non-tty), making the TUI more likely to engage / render decoratively.

This is DISTINCT from the weekly-cap "malformed API response" throttle (a real cap) — this is TUI-into-a-pipe corruption, which is fixable.

## Fix

1. Strip ANSI/OSC/control sequences from the captured claude-seat stdout (and stderr) before usability/parse — belt-and-suspenders so a stray sequence can never corrupt the verdict. Reuse the single-source ANSI regex.
2. Force a non-interactive spawn for the claude backend: `TERM=dumb`, `NO_COLOR=1`, `CI=1` in the child env so the renderer never engages decoratively. (`claude-p` itself spawns under a PTY by design; we make our captured output robust + the env hostile to decoration.)
3. Preserve all other seats and the existing API-path behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- A captured-output sample with interleaved ANSI/TUI control sequences parses to the correct verdict (strip is robust).
- The non-interactive spawn env (TERM=dumb etc.) is asserted in the claude command construction.
- Other seats unaffected.
- `python tests/smoke.py` green, ruff clean.
- Live proof: `review diff --staged -m claude:claude-opus-4-8 --pool 1` returns a CLEAN parseable verdict.

title: board: resolve seats from the shared models.yaml manifest by CAPABILITY (rig#8 consumer-side residual)

Consumer-side residual of rig-cli#8 (the manifest + cron checker landed; the acceptance criterion "consumers resolve models from the manifest by capability" is still open for the review board).

## What
The shared manifest `agent-tools/lib/contracts/models.yaml` carries per-model capability tags (`[vision, reasoning, code]`) plus `roles:` / `aliases:` maps. review-cli's board only references it loosely today (the retry.py transient-regex contract + CHANGELOG), NOT for capability-aware seat selection — its DEFAULT_BOARD seats are hardcoded byte-exact strings.

title: review-qa bot AGENT-SIDE tier: drive a BRIDGE bot (tg-ctl) agent→card→tap→answer to catch the tg-cli#98 duplicate-card class
body:
## Problem

The bot Tier-1 harness only drives the **inbound** direction (`Send:` an update → `Expect:` an outbound reply). A **bridge** bot like `tg-ctl` has the OPPOSITE load-bearing flow: the AGENT emits an AskUserQuestion/permission via a hook client (`tg-ctl ask`, reads a payload on stdin) → the daemon forwards ONE inline-button CARD to Telegram → the user TAPS → the answer flows back to the hook client's STDOUT (which unblocks the agent). The inbound inject/capture path cannot reach this loop — it has no seam to emit the agent's question or read the answer.

This is exactly where the **tg-cli#98** class of bugs lives: a re-fire of an already-answered question posting a DUPLICATE, superseded card (whose tap then reads as "expired"), and lost-tap / lost-answer (the hook client hangs, the agent never gets the answer).

## What this adds

An AGENT-SIDE tier on the existing hermetic `FakeTelegram` (UNCHANGED):

- **Config (`sut.bot`):** `ask_command` (selects the tier), `seed` (pre-boot precondition files via template tokens), `owner_id`, a configurable `sender_id` (defaults to `owner_id` — a bridge gates a tap on the owner), `ready_file`.
- **Harness seam:** `emit_question(payload)→AskHandle`, `AskHandle.await_answer()→str|None` (None/hang = tap-loss), `cards_captured()`, `tap(card,label)` (synthetic callback_query).
- **Suite grammar:** `Ask-question:`/`Ask-permission:`, `Expect-card: N`, `Tap: <label>`, `Expect-answer: <substr>`. A re-Ask with `Expect-card: 0` + `Expect-answer:` is the #98 regression assertion.

## Acceptance criteria

- A faithful miniature bridge-bot fixture verdicts PASS replaying an answered re-fire, FAILs under `SUT_DUP_BUG=1` (the #98 duplicate-card class) — driven through the REAL harness (fake Telegram + a real subprocess daemon + a real Unix-socket hook client).
- **RED→GREEN proof against the real `tg-ctl`:** the SAME suite verdicts PASS on current tg-ctl (the #98 fix) and FAIL on pre-#98 tg-ctl (271ff1d) — proving the harness catches the real bug class.
- Unit tests for the parser, config knobs, harness seam, template/seed layer, and the BLOCKED/containment paths.

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)
- Tier-2 real-tap needs test-account MTProto creds (#82/#84).
- Broader SUT-precondition generalization.

title: Fix review-cli smoke failures surfaced during visual review fix
body:
## What

A failed smoke run reported as unrelated local environment without an owner lets regressions accumulate and makes review-cli gates untrustworthy.

Agents can rely on review-cli smoke as a real go/no-go signal instead of manually interpreting known failures every time.

title: fix(install): use `command git` in pre-commit hook template to bypass shell aliases
body:
## Problem

The `_PRECOMMIT` template in `reviewlib/install.py` (installed via `review install-commit-hook`) uses bare `git` calls. Shell tools like RTK rewrite `git diff` into a compact summary format. When the installed hook runs `git diff --no-ext-diff --cached`, a shell alias/function wrapping git would produce different output than review-cli's internal hash (which uses `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` — bypassing aliases entirely).

Result: hash mismatch → hook blocks a legitimately-reviewed commit.

## Fix

Use `command git` instead of bare `git` in the template. `command` (POSIX) bypasses shell aliases and functions while still resolving the binary via PATH.

Mirrors agent-tools#155 / #156 which fixed the same issue in the `review-gate` global hook.

title: deploy.sh: fetch --prune so a deleted/renamed upstream branch is detected
body:
Follow-up to PR #106 (codex P2 review thread). `git fetch "$remote"` without `--prune` leaves a stale remote-tracking ref when the upstream branch was deleted/renamed on the remote, so `rev-parse "$upstream"` still succeeds and unattended `rig apply` reports "already up to date" instead of the documented "no upstream ref" exit-1 path.

title: visual: gate Russian-language selection/highlight claims, not just English
body:
## Problem

Alex reported (tg#6188): a HyperCanvas screenshot captioned/claimed as showing a
"selected" element (Russian: "элемент выбран") passed `review visual` even though no
selection outline was actually drawn — the deterministic CV veto that exists precisely
to catch this (`reviewlib/features/visual/contrib/selection_highlight.py`, the
`selection-highlight` contributed module) never activated.

## Root cause

Module activation from free-text `--intent` (`ContributedModule.activates` in
`registry.py`, and the contrib module's own standalone `activates`) matched the
`activates_on` tag ("selection") as a raw English substring against the intent text.
A Russian caption never contains the literal string "selection", so the module stayed
inactive and the render fell through to the generic style/blank/error-overlay built-ins
— none of which ask about a selection frame at all — letting the false claim pass as
`keep`.

(Separately, and out of scope for this issue: the `tg` pre-send-photo hook does not
currently forward the outgoing photo's caption as `--intent` at all, so this whole
intent-driven activation path is inert for tg-sent screenshots regardless of language —
tracked in the `tg-cli` repo.)

## Fix

Add `reviewlib/features/visual/intent_keywords.py`: a small tag -> synonym map
(English + Russian: выбран/выделен/подсвечен/рамка выделения) consulted by both
intent-activation call sites instead of a bare tag substring check. Only ADDS matches
(consistent with intent being allowed to tighten activation, never loosen it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `MODULE.activates(ctx)` returns True for a Russian intent claiming selection
      (e.g. "элемент выбран", "элемент выделен рамкой", "элемент подсвечен",
      "видна рамка выделения") for the `selection-highlight` module.
- [ ] The `selection-highlight` module's `cv_check` still BLOCKs when a Russian-intent
      claim is paired with a render that has no selection outline, and PASSes when the
      outline is present (end-to-end regression, not just unit-level activation).
- [ ] Existing English-intent activation behavior is unchanged (no regression).

## Proof

`tests/test_intent_keywords.py`, plus Russian-intent cases added to
`tests/test_selection_highlight.py` and `tests/test_visual_registry.py`.

title: review diff --commit: safe checkpoint for multi-round fix loops (never git reset --hard)
body:
## What's wrong

An agent iterating a review -> fix findings -> re-review loop needs a safe way to undo
a bad attempt. The only tool available was `git reset --hard`, which discards ALL
uncommitted changes in the working tree -- including uncommitted work belonging to a
DIFFERENT session/agent sharing the same checkout.

## Evidence / where it came from

This happened in production today (2026-07-04): a subagent iterating a
`review diff --staged` fix-loop ran `git reset --hard` mid-loop to discard a bad
attempt, and it wiped uncommitted work belonging to a different session/agent sharing
the same checkout. Data was recovered, but the repo owner asked for (1) an explicit
warning against this pattern in review-cli's own docs/help, and (2) a safer checkpoint
primitive.

## User impact

Without this, any agent-driven review-fix-loop that needs to discard a bad attempt has
no safe undo mechanism inside review-cli itself, and reaches for `git reset --hard` by
default -- which is destructive to shared checkouts (worktrees used by multiple parallel
agents/sessions on the same machine).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `review diff --staged --commit` creates a real `git commit` checkpoint of the
      reviewed staged diff after the review completes.
- [ ] `--commit` without `--staged` is a hard usage error (distinct exit code), never a
      silent no-op and never an implicit `--staged`.
- [ ] The checkpoint gate mirrors the existing `--staged` commit-hook stamp gate exactly
      (ok / staged / not-piped-stdin) -- a review with open findings still gets
      checkpointed, since "ok" means the pool produced usable verdicts, not "zero
      findings".
- [ ] A `git commit` hook rejection (commit-msg/pre-commit) fails `--commit` loudly with
      its own distinct exit code, never silently swallowed and never bypassed with
      `--no-verify`.
- [ ] README.md / AGENTS.md / `review --help` explicitly warn against `git reset --hard`
      mid-review-cycle and name the safe alternatives (`git checkout -- <file>`,
      `review diff --staged --commit` + `git reset --soft HEAD~1`).

## Notes

Branch: `feat/review-diff-commit-checkpoint`. Tests:
`tests/test_review_commit_checkpoint.py` (7 cases) + a CLI-level E2E smoke test in
`tests/smoke.py`.

comments.body:
## Follow-up findings from dogfooding this feature's own PR (not fixed here — deferred with rationale)

Ran `review diff --staged --commit` on this feature's own diff (twice, across two rounds
of changes) as a real-world test. Two rounds of AI review findings came back; documenting
the ones NOT fixed inline, so this doesn't turn into a never-terminating fix-loop (which
is exactly the failure mode this feature exists to make safe from).

**Fixed inline (this PR):**
- TOCTOU guard: `--commit` now re-reads the staged diff immediately before committing and
  refuses (`EXIT_COMMIT_FAILED`) if it drifted from what was actually reviewed (a review is
  multi-minute; another process/session sharing the checkout could stage more in the
  meantime). See `_current_staged_diff` / `_checkpoint_commit` in `reviewlib/modes/review.py`.
- Test hygiene: `tests/test_review_commit_checkpoint.py`'s env sandbox now redirects
  `REVIEW_MARKER`/`HOME` (mirrors `test_review_marker.py`), so running the file standalone
  no longer mutates the developer's real `~/.cache/agent-tools/last-review`.

**Deferred (tracked here, not fixed):**

1. **Residual check-then-commit gap.** Even after the TOCTOU guard above, there's still a
   small window between the drift-check subprocess and the `git commit` subprocess. Closing
   it fully would mean committing an immutable snapshot via `git commit-tree` instead of
   porcelain `git commit` — but `commit-tree` SKIPS commit-msg/pre-commit hooks entirely,
   which conflicts with this feature's hard requirement that the checkpoint runs the repo's
   own hooks and never bypasses them. Accepted trade-off: the window narrowed from MINUTES
   (the whole multi-model review) to milliseconds (subprocess handoff) — as tight as normal
   `git commit` allows without giving up hook enforcement. Revisit only if someone actually
   hits this in practice.

2. **Stamp/marker ordering vs. drift.** `_stamp_if_staged_commit_review` (the pre-existing
   `--staged` review-stamp + agent-tools marker) is written BEFORE `--commit`'s internal
   `git commit` call — and this order is REQUIRED: on a machine with the
   `require-review-before-commit` global git hook installed, `--commit`'s own internal
   commit is itself subject to that hook, and it only passes because the stamp/marker were
   just written by the same review run. I tried reordering so the stamp is skipped when
   drift is detected (to avoid a stale "this diff was reviewed" signal surviving a refused
   checkpoint) — confirmed by testing that this BREAKS `--commit` on any machine with that
   hook installed (the internal commit then fails the same gate a human's commit would,
   because the stamp/marker aren't there yet). Reverted.
   The underlying concern (a diff-hash-stamped record could, via the marker's mtime-only
   check, let some OTHER later out-of-band commit sail through unreviewed if the index
   drifted) is a property of the pre-existing stamp/marker + external-hook contract, not
   something `--commit` introduces — a plain `review --staged` (no `--commit` at all) has
   the identical exposure today. If it needs fixing, it should happen in the stamp/marker
   design itself (e.g. making the external hook always verify the diff-hash stamp, never
   just the marker mtime) or in the external `agent-tools` hook, not by reordering
   `--commit`'s own call sequence, which breaks the feature's happy path.

title: visual: vision-judge check for visible error/exception/fail text anywhere in a screenshot
body:
## What
Add a new boolean field (error_text_visible) to the SAME single vision-LLM judge call review's --visual pipeline already makes (alongside unstyled/blank/error_overlay), implemented as a new built-in VisualModule in reviewlib/features/visual/modules/builtins.py. Unlike the 3 existing built-ins, there is no pixel-level CV signal for this (cv_check returns None, no CV opinion) — it is a pure semantic vision-judgment call: ask the model whether any visible text anywhere in the image (a console/log panel entry, a stack trace, a dev-server error banner, or elsewhere in the UI) reads as an actual error/failure diagnostic (error, exception, fail(ure), crash, traceback, 404/not-found), as opposed to a benign occurrence of those words (a filename, a doc string, a '0 errors' summary label). When true, the module judge()s a hard 'block' veto exactly like error_overlay=true does today, rolling back the verdict in the standalone review visual / --strict / tg --photo-hook path. Wires in automatically via the existing builtin_modules() list consumed by both pipeline.py and compose.py.

## Why (motivation)
Alex (tg#6850): add to review visual an OCR searching for stop-words error/exception/fail/failure etc — probably a vision-LLM judge is how this should work. Trigger: HyperIDE's own built-in HYPER LOGS diagnostics panel showed a real React Router ErrorBoundary 404 entry in a screenshot, and review's existing visual gate (unstyled/blank/error_overlay) did not catch it because none of those 3 checks look at arbitrary on-screen TEXT — they only catch layout-level breakage (no CSS, blank canvas, a big red compile-error banner). A real runtime error rendered as plain log/console text slips through today.

> **tg#6850** — Alex, 2026-07-05 11:24 UTC: И добавь в review visual ocr ищущий стоп слова error exception fail failure и тп. наверно это как visual LLM должно рабо…
<!-- tasklib:msgref-quote:6850 -->

## User impact
Anyone using 'review visual --strict' or the 'tg --photo' pre-send hook to gate screenshots gets an extra safety net: a screenshot containing visible error/exception/failure text anywhere on screen (not just a big red overlay) is now flagged and blocked instead of silently passing as a 'keep'.

## Cost of inaction
The exact miss that prompted this ticket recurs: a real, user-visible runtime error rendered as plain text in a log/console panel (rather than a full-screen dev-server overlay) continues to slip past review's visual gate and get shipped/sent as a 'looks fine' screenshot.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New ErrorTextModule in the visual builtins module: cv_check always returns None (no CV signal exists for this), vision_questions contributes the error_text_visible prompt, judge() returns decision=block when the vision verdict's error_text_visible answer is True, abstain otherwise
- [ ] The built-in modules list includes the new module, so it activates by default on every --visual run in both the standalone pipeline (hard veto) and the companion --visual fan-out (folded into the grounded note as today's error_overlay does)
- [ ] Unit tests: mocked vision verdict with error_text_visible=True causes the module judge to block; =False (or absent-but-schema-valid) does not block
- [ ] Pipeline-level test: running the full pipeline with a mocked vision call returning error_text_visible=True ends in a final rollback verdict; =False does not roll back on that basis
- [ ] Docs updated (built-ins lists) and a changelog entry added referencing this issue number

## What
tests/test_preclassifier.py::test_pipeline_check_run_does_not_reuse_plain_keep runs run_pipeline() twice (plain, then with requested_checks=['selection']) with NO RegistryEnv override, unlike tests/test_visual_registry.py which monkeypatches the registry's trust/global-registry/audit paths before calling run_pipeline. On a machine where ~/.config/review-cli/modules.json / global-visual-modules.json globally registers the real selection-highlight contributed module (activates_on includes 'selection'), the second run's requested_checks=['selection'] makes the pipeline load and run the REAL contributed module (trust-by-default), whose cv_check correctly vetoes the synthetic fixture (no real 2px selection outline) and rolls back BEFORE any vision call. The test asserts the second run still calls vision (log2 == ['gemini']) expecting a plain cache-miss escalation, so it fails with log2 == [] and a rollback verdict instead. Confirmed on a clean origin/main worktree with zero other changes, so this is 100% pre-existing and environment-dependent (present whenever the global manifest exists on the host running the suite), not something a CI runner without that global file would ever see. Fix: isolate the registry env in this test the same way test_visual_registry.py already does (monkeypatch RegistryEnv/_default_trust_path/_default_global_registry_path/_default_audit_path to a throwaway tmp dir for the duration of the test), so the test exercises only the built-in modules regardless of what is globally registered on the host machine.

## Why (motivation)
Discovered incidentally while verifying review-cli#121 (the new error-text visual module): the full guardrail test run (tests/test_policy_engine.py, test_preclassifier.py, test_vision_client.py, test_selection_highlight.py, test_visual_registry.py) showed exactly one failure, reproduced identically on a pristine origin/main checkout with none of the #121 changes present, so it is unrelated to that PR. Root cause traced to the global module registration added 2026-07-04 (global-visual-modules.json, 'Registered globally 2026-07-04 after discovering it was implemented+tested but never wired into any manifest anywhere on this machine') which this one pre-existing test never accounted for.

## User impact
Anyone running 'python tests/smoke.py' or this test file locally on a machine that has ever run 'review register-module' for a selection-tagged contributed module gets a spurious local test failure that CI (a clean runner with no such global file) will never show — eroding trust in local test runs and wasting time re-diagnosing a false regression on every future local run.

## Cost of inaction
The next person (or agent) who runs the local test suite on this or a similarly-configured machine burns time re-diagnosing what looks like a real regression, exactly as happened here, every single time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] test_pipeline_check_run_does_not_reuse_plain_keep (and any sibling test_preclassifier.py test that calls run_pipeline with requested_checks or otherwise exercises module selection) isolates the visual-module registry the same way test_visual_registry.py does, so it passes regardless of the host's real ~/.config/review-cli global registration state

title: Companion --visual (review diff/brainstorm/quorum --visual) never hard-vetoes on ANY built-in module block, only the standalone pipeline does
body:
## What
reviewlib/features/visual/compose.py's build_mode_visual_context/_run_fanout path (the companion --visual fan-out used by 'review diff --visual', 'review brainstorm --visual', 'review quorum --visual') gathers the active built-in modules' vision_questions and folds the model's module_answers into a text note for the companion text-mode reviewers to read, but it NEVER calls module.judge() and never runs the module veto / decide_from_vision policy engine step that the standalone 'review visual IMAGE' pipeline (pipeline.py) applies. So a companion run whose vision result comes back with, e.g., error_overlay=true, blank=true, unstyled=true, or (as of review-cli#121) error_text_visible=true does NOT hard-block the companion text mode the way 'review visual --strict' would -- reviewlib/cli.py only blocks the companion mode on a cvGate rollback or a genuinely-unusable/unavailable vision result (see cli.py around the build_mode_visual_context call site), not on a module-level block. This is PRE-EXISTING behavior for all 4 built-in modules (style-presence, blank-frame, error-overlay, and now error-text) -- not introduced by #121 -- surfaced during that PR's multi-model review (Codex flagged it as P1 scoped only to error-text, but verification traced it to being a general compose.py-vs-pipeline.py architecture split that predates this PR).

## Why (motivation)
Surfaced by review-cli#121's own 'review diff' self-review (Codex reviewer, P1 finding), while implementing the new error-text visual module. Deliberately NOT fixed inside #121: making compose.py enforce the same hard veto pipeline.py does is a real product/architecture decision (does 'review diff --visual' become strict-by-default the same way 'review visual --strict' is?) that changes behavior for the 3 EXISTING built-ins too, not just the new one -- out of scope for a 'add one field to the vision judge' change and needs its own deliberate design pass.

## User impact
A user running 'review diff --visual shot.png' or 'review brainstorm ... --visual shot.png' gets a companion text-mode answer even when the attached screenshot has a confirmed dev-server error overlay, a blank canvas, an unstyled render, or now visible error/exception text -- the vision model's answer is folded into the prompt as a note for the text reviewers to (hopefully) notice, but nothing enforces it, unlike the standalone 'review visual --strict' / 'tg --photo' hook paths which DO hard-block on the exact same module answers.

## Cost of inaction
The gap stays invisible: users assume any --visual-carrying review command enforces the same built-in safety checks, when only the standalone pipeline actually does -- exactly the kind of silent miss review-cli#121 itself was filed to close for on-screen error text specifically.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A deliberate decision is recorded (ticket comment or a follow-up doc note) on whether compose.py's companion fan-out should run the same module veto policy_engine.decide_from_vision applies, and if so, implement it with an end-to-end test (fake a module_answers block=True answer, assert the companion mode is blocked/refused) for at least one of the 4 built-ins
- [ ] If the decision is 'not now', the docs (README.md / architecture-visual-verification.md) explicitly say companion --visual folds module answers as advisory context only and does not hard-block, so this is a documented trade-off rather than a silent gap

title: self-merge-authority quorum: should non-review modes (brainstorm/quorum/just-ask) count toward the gate at all
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Raised by an automated review pass on the [#136](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/136) fix (ran-vs-passed verdict gating for review task --check): the reviewer flagged that reviewlib/modes/brainstorm.py can exit 0 after a mid-run collapse (some rounds died, partial synthesis still produced), and #136 intentionally still records that as passed=True since brainstorm has no PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict grammar to decouple from (unlike qa, which #136 does exclude) -- but whether brainstorm/quorum/just-ask should count toward a review-focused self-merge-authority gate at all was never decided

## User impact
Without a decision, the quorum gate's iteration count keeps mixing review-diff verdicts with brainstorm/quorum/just-ask runs whose passed semantics are looser or nonexistent, which could let a degraded brainstorm nudge a task toward satisfying --min-iter/--min-models for what is meant to be an independent-review gate

## Cost of inaction
The self-merge-authority gate's iteration count keeps an implicit, undocumented policy (every mode counts, brainstorm's partial success counts as a pass) instead of an explicit CTO decision

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide and document whether review task CODE --check should only count mode==review iterations toward --min-iter/--min-models, or continue aggregating every task-coded mode (review/quorum/just-ask/brainstorm/qa) as it does today
- [ ] If non-review modes stay in scope, decide per-mode what a fair passed signal is -- e.g. brainstorm's exit 0 on a mid-run dead-panel collapse (documented partial-success behavior, CTO 2026-06-16) currently counts as passed under the ran-vs-passed fix in issue #136, which is defensible but debatable since the panel degraded

comments.body:
Additional finding from a later review pass on #136 (same PR): the exit-code-based
\`passed\` signal has a limitation for \`review\` (diff review) mode specifically, not
just the non-review modes this issue was filed about.

\`reviewlib/modes/review.py\`'s exit code (\`ok = all(r.returncode == 0 for r in
results)\`) means "every reviewer's backend call completed technically" — NOT "every
reviewer approved the diff with no findings". review-cli's text-panel reviewers print
free-text findings with no structured accept/reject/severity grammar to parse (unlike
\`qa\`'s PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict, which #136 does thread correctly by excluding it).
So a reviewer that ran cleanly and printed "found 3 blocking issues" still records
\`passed=True\` and counts toward \`review task CODE --check\`'s \`--min-iter\`/
\`--min-models\` today.

#136 still closes the gap the CTO decision (tg#7306 #1) actually targeted — a review
round that technically FAILED to run (backend error, timeout, degraded board) no
longer counts, which was the literal gaming vector described ("3 shallow/failing
reviews"). But "ran cleanly with findings" vs "ran cleanly with no findings" is a
different, deeper gap: it would need a real content verdict for review mode (parsing
model output for an approve/block signal), which doesn't exist anywhere in review-cli
today and is a substantially larger change than #136's "ran vs passed (via exit code)"
scope.

Documented inline at the \`mode == "qa"\` branch in \`_run_mode_with_stats\`
(\`reviewlib/cli.py\`). Rolling this into this issue's decision scope since it's the
same underlying question (what should "passed" mean per mode) — worth deciding
together with the brainstorm/non-review-mode question already filed here.

Plan for a narrower, adjacent fix in this same area (not resolving this issue's own two open questions — mode-counting policy and review mode's free-text content-verdict gap, both of which remain open and undecided):

Alex hit this concretely: Opus review OK; Codex/GLM/Grok/Sonnet quota-exhausted -> could not record 3 review iterations. Root cause: an exact `-m modelA,modelB,modelC,...` board (no reserve to backfill a failed seat) records per-seat role data (`roles`), but `_run_mode_with_stats`'s `passed` is the WHOLE run's own all-or-nothing verdict, and `quorum_check` only ever reads `roles` from a `passed is True` record — so ONE hard-failed sibling seat (nonzero returncode from a quota-exhausted provider) zeroes out role credit for the ENTIRE iteration, including a seat (e.g. Opus) that genuinely produced a verdict.

Fix: make ROLE credit seat-granular while leaving `passed`/`--min-iter`/`--min-models` exactly as they are today (still run-level, all-or-nothing):

- `record_run` gains a new `usable_roles` param — the roles of seats that INDIVIDUALLY produced a usable verdict this run (`panel.FailoverOutcome.usable_roles`), written regardless of the run's own `passed`. No `models`-length-alignment requirement (unlike the existing `roles` field) — it's simply "the roles this run actually satisfied".
- `cli._run_mode_with_stats` threads a new `usable_roles_after` callable (mirroring `models_after`/`roles_after`), wired in `_dispatch` to `outcome_sink[0].usable_roles` for the review/visual board path — the SAME source the existing NON-exact (reserve-failover) `roles_after` already reads, with no exact-board special case needed since `FailoverOutcome.usable_roles` already means "seats that individually succeeded" either way.
- `stats.quorum_check`'s `--min-roles` gate credits from a new `_seat_credited_roles` helper: reads `usable_roles` when present (falling back to the legacy passed-only `roles` reading for pre-fix records), across every non-diff-identity-mismatched iteration regardless of that iteration's own `passed`.
- Regression test: 3 seats recorded in one run, 1 usable (role=correctness), 2 quota-exhausted (rc!=0) — `quorum_check` must credit "correctness" despite `passed=False` for the whole run.

Not in scope here (left for this issue's own decision): whether brainstorm/quorum/just-ask should count toward the gate at all, and review mode's free-text content-verdict parsing. PR incoming, will reference this issue (not "Fixes #137" — your two acceptance criteria above are unrelated and stay open).

title: review pool: gemini-2.5-flash seat 404s (stale model) — counts as a dispatched-but-empty reviewer in quorum
body:
## What
During ship-gate review-quorum runs on 2026-07-09 (PRs [#650](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas/pull/650) [HYP-948](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-948), [#651](https://github.com/hyperide/hyper-saas/pull/651) [HYP-960](https://linear.app/glide-vc/issue/HYP-960), hatch stack task 213), the gemini seat repeatedly failed with a 404 on model `gemini-2.5-flash` (a stale/retired model id), the Kimi/commandcode seats failed on out-of-credits, and GLM timed out. Only codex returned substantive reviews. Yet the structural review-quorum gate counts a reviewer that DISPATCHED, not one that RETURNED a substantive review — so a 404'd/failed seat still counts toward the `>=3 distinct models` bar. A PR can therefore appear to meet quorum while only 1 model actually reviewed. Two parts: (1) Update the gemini model id in the review pool config to a current, non-404 model (verify the correct current Gemini model name), and in the same sweep check the other seats (Kimi/commandcode credits, GLM timeout) and either fix them or mark them clearly as optional / best-effort so a dead seat does not silently inflate the quorum count. (2) The quorum count should require a SUBSTANTIVE completion, not mere dispatch. [PR #138](https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/138) (verdict recording: passed vs ran) is the related fix already in flight; this ticket's config half (correct model ids) is complementary and can land independently. Do not implement here — ticket only.

## Why (motivation)
The self-merge review-quorum gate that Alex mandated for agent self-merge (>=3 distinct models) can currently be satisfied largely by seats that never actually reviewed. On 2026-07-09 real ship-gate runs, only codex returned a substantive review while gemini 404'd on a stale model id, Kimi/commandcode ran out of credits, and GLM timed out — but the gate still treated them as participating reviewers.

## User impact
Agents rely on the review-quorum gate as the guarantee before self-merging PRs. Today that guarantee is hollow: the >=3-distinct-models bar can be met by seats that 404, run out of credits, or time out without ever producing a review, so PRs merge on an illusory quorum.

## Cost of inaction
Agents keep self-merging on a hollow quorum. The gate's central guarantee — that at least 3 distinct models actually reviewed the diff — is illusory, and bad changes can ship past a gate everyone believes is protecting them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The gemini seat runs without a 404 on a current, valid Gemini model id (config updated and verified).
- [ ] A seat that errors / 404s / times out / is out of credits is NOT counted toward the distinct-models quorum bar, or is at minimum clearly logged as a non-counting failure so the quorum count reflects only substantive completions.
- [ ] The other pool seats (Kimi/commandcode credits, GLM timeout) are either fixed or explicitly marked optional / best-effort so a dead seat cannot silently inflate the quorum count.

title: opencode oc:zai/glm-5.2 seat HANGS (zero output), wedging the entire diff review pool
body:
## What
The default diff-review roster (config.yaml models:) includes the agentic opencode seat oc:zai glm-5.2. When z.ai quota is exhausted the opencode agentic path does NOT fail fast, it HANGS with zero output. Observed live: pid 65987 hung 16+ minutes and pid 64399 also stuck, both 'opencode run --agent read-only-reviewer -m zai glm-5.2'. Because the pool waits on all its seats, one hung glm seat stalls the whole review diff run. During a fleet run of ~10 concurrent review-cli-gated ship agents this throttled review throughput across the fleet. The keyed-HTTP zai glm-5.2 backend and the opencode oc zai path share the same exhausted z.ai quota, but the REST path fails fast while the agentic opencode path hangs.

## Why (motivation)
review-cli is the shared merge gate for a fleet of concurrent ship agents; a single hanging seat serializes/stalls every review that includes it, directly cutting fleet throughput.

## User impact
Agents running review diff wait many minutes (up to the full 300s+ timeout) per review because the glm opencode seat hangs; ~10 concurrent agents were throttled.

## Cost of inaction
Every fleet run that includes the glm seat keeps wedging on it; reviewers stack up, ship throughput drops, and operators must manually kill hung opencode procs. The mitigation applied now (glm seat commented out of the diff roster in the config) is a local workaround, not a code fix; the hang-instead-of-fail-fast behavior remains for any oc seat whose provider quota is exhausted.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An unresponsive/hanging opencode agentic seat is bounded by a hard per-seat watchdog so it can never stall the pool beyond a short cap (a fast first-token/liveness timeout distinct from the full review timeout).
- [ ] When z.ai (or any provider) quota is exhausted, the oc provider seat fails fast (skipped or failed-over) instead of hanging with zero output.
- [ ] A review diff with a dead/hanging glm seat completes on the remaining pool within the configured timeout, with the glm seat reported as failed rather than silently pending.

title: review-cli leaks model child processes on kill/timeout (orphaned reviewer subprocesses survive)
body:
## What
When a review run is killed or hits its timeout, review-cli does not reliably reap the model-runner subprocesses it spawned. Observed live: an orphaned 'claude --print ... --model claude-opus-4-8' review-model process (pid 11290, ppid=1) was still alive 3h37m after its run ended. Each heavy backend (codex/claude/opencode) spawns a model-runner subprocess (and those spawn grandchildren); on abnormal termination the process group / child tree is not fully killed, so orphans reparent to init (ppid=1) and linger. Over a long fleet session these accumulate and consume CPU/RAM/quota.

## Why (motivation)
Long fleet sessions run and cancel many reviews; leaked reviewer processes accumulate, wasting CPU/RAM and (for keyed backends) burning API quota with no owner to reap them.

## User impact
Operators find multi-hour-old orphaned reviewer processes (e.g. claude-opus-4-8 pid 11290 alive 3.5h) that must be manually hunted and killed; machine load creeps up over a session.

## Cost of inaction
Every killed/timed-out review potentially leaks a subprocess tree; across a long multi-agent session orphans pile up until the machine is degraded and someone manually pkills them. The existing process.py _kill_tree/pgid machinery exists but is evidently not invoked on all termination paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On timeout or kill of a review run, all spawned model-runner subprocesses AND their descendants are terminated (kill the whole process group / tree, verify no ppid=1 orphans remain).
- [ ] A stress test that starts and hard-kills review runs repeatedly leaves zero surviving reviewer subprocesses afterward.
- [ ] Cleanup is registered so it runs on SIGTERM/SIGINT and on the internal per-seat timeout path, not only on normal exit.

title: review-cli: log/jobs dir write denied inside a sandboxed caller kills the whole seat (Fable/claude-p exit 127)
body:
## What
When `review diff --pool N` runs a Claude/Fable seat (`claude:claude-fable-5`, role architect) from INSIDE a Claude Code subagent's sandboxed Bash environment, that seat fails with:

```
[exit 127] Operation not permitted: ~/Library/Logs/review-cli/*.log
```

`log_dir()` (and `jobs.jobs_dir()` for `--detach`) either `mkdir`s the OS-standard log location or opens a per-call log file there. A sandboxed caller (an agent harness's restricted Bash tool, a locked-down CI runner) commonly denies writes outside the system temp dir — `~/Library/Logs` / `$XDG_STATE_HOME` / `~/.cache` live outside most sandbox allow-lists. The `PermissionError`/`OSError` was raised straight out of `_run_streamed` BEFORE the backend subprocess was even spawned, killing that seat entirely. Every seat (opus/codex/fable/opencode) hits the identical `_open_log -> log_dir` path, so this was never actually fable-specific — fable is simply the slowest seat (~15 min) and so the most likely to still be running when a time-scoped sandbox grant narrows.

Confirmed recurring across at least 6 separate review runs in one session (M2/#665, #126, #664, #667, #304 in the consuming repo). Current workaround: disable the subagent's sandbox specifically for the review call — fragile, forgotten repeatedly.

## Why (motivation)
Multiple concurrent agents depend on `review diff` finishing all pool seats. A seat crashing on its own logging is an self-inflicted, entirely avoidable failure — the log file is a nice-to-have transcript artifact, not the review result itself.

## User impact
A review pool loses a seat (often the architect/Fable seat) every time it's invoked from inside a sandboxed subagent, degrading review quality/coverage and forcing a manual retry with the sandbox disabled.

## Cost of inaction
Every sandboxed subagent call to `review diff --pool >=2` risks losing a seat; agents keep re-discovering and re-applying the same manual workaround instead of it being fixed once in the tool.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `log_dir()` falls back to a guaranteed-writable temp dir (keyed by uid) when the standard OS log location can't be created, printing which path it used to stderr (not swallowing the condition silently). — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/gh162-proof.txt)
- [x] The per-call log FILE open (when the dir already exists but isn't writable) also falls back, via `_open_log_with_fallback`. — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/gh162-proof.txt)
- [x] `jobs.jobs_dir()` (the `--detach` companion) gets the same fallback, since its job-record write is subject to the identical sandboxed-write denial. — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/gh162-proof.txt)
- [x] Unit tests reproduce the failure with a `chmod 0o000` directory/file (no sandbox harness needed) and assert `_run_streamed` still runs the backend and returns a real result instead of raising. — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/gh162-proof.txt)
- [x] Manual repro: confirmed no longer hits exit 127 when driven from inside a Claude Code subagent's sandboxed Bash tool. — proof: ![proof](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ultra-xp-rig-cli/89e7f5e9-4808-41e8-bf8b-0a8b213b7c89/scratchpad/gh162-proof/criterion5-proof.txt)
