title: One exhausted Claude account blocks every claude:* seat regardless of which account is active
body:
## What

review-cli's `usage_limits.py` aggregates the WORST `used_percent` across EVERY Claude Code
account `harness limits --all --json` discovers on the machine (`_percent_from_harness_cards`
has no account filter), so one exhausted or misreported account blocks EVERY `claude:*` seat
(`opus`/`sonnet`/`fable`) even when the account actually configured/active for the dispatch is
fine.

## Incident (2026-09-09)

Alex's hatch-request: every configured review seat reported exhausted simultaneously (Claude 5h
window 100%, Codex until Sep 15, z.ai weekly until Sep 10, Grok out of credits, commandcode
unpaid, Gemini disabled) despite this machine having multiple live Claude accounts
(`~/.claude-accounts/account-0/1/2`, managed by `~/.files/bin/claude-rotate`) and omp's own
ability to host Claude models through a separate auth path.

## Fix

- `reviewlib/claude_accounts.py` (new): discovers the existing `~/.claude-accounts/account-*`
  registry (the same layout `claude-rotate`/`harness-cli` already use).
- `usage_limits.py`: `allow_spawn_for_model`/`spawn_refuse_reason`/etc. gain an `account=` filter
  so a card for a DIFFERENT account never gates a dispatch for the account actually in use.
- `backends.py`: `review_claude`'s CLI transport rotates across registered accounts
  (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) before giving up; `review_omp` gains a parallel profile-rotation axis
  (`$REVIEW_OMP_CLAUDE_PROFILES`) for omp-hosted Claude models.
- `config.py`: new `OMP_CLAUDE_SEAT` (`omp:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) board seat -- a genuinely
  different auth path (omp's own credentials) than the direct `claude:*` CLI seats, so it
  survives an outage that takes out every `claude:*` seat's shared account state.

## Residual gap

Omp currently has exactly ONE working Claude identity on this machine; a second
`$REVIEW_OMP_CLAUDE_PROFILES` entry needs a one-time human interactive OAuth login. If literally
every configured Claude account AND the omp default are simultaneously exhausted (observed live
during this incident), the fallback chain still bottoms out -- same as any finite fallback list.

title: SQLite-backed durable call/brainstorm log archive

## What
Add reviewlib/log_archive.py (chunked, zstd/zlib-compressed SQLite store for review-cli call and brainstorm logs) and reviewlib/log_archive_migrate.py (one-shot migration + 4-proof verification), then wire reviewlib/process.py (call recording) and reviewlib/dashboard/parser.py (session loading) to write to and read from the archive when REVIEW_LOG_SQLITE is enabled (default on). Tests that assert on live on-disk .log files (test_dashboard.py, test_streaming.py, test_true_silence_cooldown_wiring.py) opt out via REVIEW_LOG_SQLITE=0.

The live log dir (~/Library/Logs/review-cli) has grown to ~154k small files / 4.4GB+ (review-cli#447, review-cli#466): every review stat and dashboard cold start re-parses tens of thousands of files, and the old derived-data cache duplicated full bodies without ever shrinking the source dir. Anyone running review-cli's dashboard or review stat on a long-lived install currently pays O(total historical file count) on every scan/parse; a bounded chunked store keeps this fast as the corpus grows instead of degrading indefinitely.

The log directory keeps growing unboundedly (already 4.4GB/154k files) and dashboard/stat latency keeps degrading with it (review-cli#447).

title: stats.py stalled-models diagnostic misses omp seat true-silence cooldowns (ACCESS_METHODS missing "omp")
body:
## What
`review --check`'s "stalled_models" diagnostic (`reviewlib/stats.py`, ~line 1783) iterates `_seat_cooldown.ACCESS_METHODS` to discover which access method a model is cooling down under. PR #478 (review-cli#235's omp half) added a new `_OMP_ACCESS_METHOD = "omp"` cooldown namespace in `reviewlib/backends.py` for `review_omp`'s true-silence cooldown record/consult calls, but `reviewlib/seat_cooldown.ACCESS_METHODS` (currently `("cli", "api", "opencode")`) was never updated to include `"omp"`.

## Why (motivation)
Found while independently verifying PR #478's true-silence fix while investigating this session's `-m mimo` (`omp:opencode-go/mimo-v2.5`) hang. `review_omp`'s own dispatch path is correct — its pre-dispatch skip and post-dispatch record/clear call `active_cooldown`/`record_cooldown`/`clear_cooldown` directly with `access_method="omp"` (a hardcoded literal, not routed through the `ACCESS_METHODS` tuple), so the actual hang fix and cooldown-gated redispatch protection both work. The gap is scoped to exactly one consumer: `reviewlib/stats.py`'s stalled-models diagnostic, which probes `ACCESS_METHODS` generically because it doesn't know in advance which transport a given model dispatches through.

## User impact
After an omp seat (e.g. `-m mimo`) goes true-silent and gets cooldown-recorded, `review --check` on a task whose review bar wasn't met silently omits that seat from `stalled_models` — a user debugging "why didn't this task pass review" sees no explanation for a cooling-down omp seat, even though `review diff`'s own dispatch correctly skips it and would show the skip in its own per-call log.

## Cost of inaction
Every omp-seat true-silence cooldown is invisible to this one diagnostic surface indefinitely. This is a growing blind spot now that MiMo 2.5 (`config.py`'s `MIMO_SEAT = "omp:opencode-go/mimo-v2.5"`) is a default board seat reachable via the short `-m mimo` alias.

## Cost of inaction
See above.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `reviewlib/seat_cooldown.ACCESS_METHODS` includes `"omp"` alongside `"cli"`, `"api"`, `"opencode"`
- [ ] a regression test records an omp-seat true-silence cooldown via `record_cooldown(model, ..., access_method="omp")` and then asserts the model appears in `compute_task_check_result`'s (or the equivalent stats.py entry point's) `stalled_models` output

## Screenshots
(none — text/data diagnostic bug, no UI)

## Links
- review-cli#235 (parent: extending true-silence detection beyond review_opencode)
- review-cli#478 (the PR that introduced `_OMP_ACCESS_METHOD` without updating `ACCESS_METHODS`)

title: review diff hangs indefinitely on 3d-cli worktree that modifies rig.yaml (possible UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT env-inheritance issue)
body:
## What
review diff --task <code> -m omp:anthropic/claude-opus-4-8[,omp:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5] invoked from /Users/ultra/.config/superpowers/worktrees/3d-cli/roadmap-gate-venv-fix (a worktree whose staged fix modifies 3d-cli's own rig.yaml to pin UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv, plus tests/run_gate.py and tests/test_run_gate.py) hung indefinitely: 0.0% CPU, zero stdout/stderr, for 20-29 minutes each time (past review-cli's own 20-minute idle floor), reproduced 3 times (twice back-to-back, once after a 7-minute cooldown), with no error and no completion.

## Why (motivation)
Diagnose and fix so review diff does not hang forever on PRs that themselves touch rig.yaml/venv config - this currently blocks shipping any such PR through review-cli's review-quorum gate.

Evidence gathered: no stale lock file was found (checked ~/.config/review-cli/.seat-cooldown.json.lock via lsof, and per-worktree .review-cli lock files) - this does NOT look like the recently-fixed hang-timeout bug's original stale-lock trigger, and does NOT look like the account-quota-exhaustion issue either (review-cli's harness was otherwise healthy system-wide during this window: ~143/199 OK on other concurrent invocations from sibling agents in the same session, including other 3d-cli PRs which shipped fine via the same omp: route).

Hypothesis (unconfirmed, worth investigating): the specific worktree/PR under review modifies rig.yaml itself, including pinning UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv - possible that review-cli's subprocess (or a git/uv call it shells out to while diffing/reading the PR's own rig.yaml) inherits or reads the modified worktree's env/rig.yaml in a way that causes a venv-resolution loop or blocking wait, distinct from normal operation.

Repro path is currently a live worktree if still present: /Users/ultra/.config/superpowers/worktrees/3d-cli/roadmap-gate-venv-fix (PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/3d-cli/pull/38).

## User impact
Blocks shipping any PR that itself modifies rig.yaml/venv-related config, via review-cli's review-quorum gate, until diagnosed. Any agent/developer whose PR touches rig.yaml or UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT cannot get a review diff verdict and is stuck.

## Cost of inaction
PRs touching rig.yaml/venv config remain permanently unshippable through the review-quorum gate (the hang never times out on its own within observed 20-29 minute windows), silently wasting agent/session time on every retry until someone hits this exact combination and manually diagnoses it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root cause of the hang is identified (or ruled out to a specific alternate cause) and documented on the ticket.
- [ ] Either a fix ships that prevents review diff from hanging on a worktree that modifies rig.yaml/UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, or a documented timeout/fail-fast is added so this scenario errors out instead of hanging indefinitely.

- [x] Phase 0 `review entities [--json]` delivered a read-only report sourced from existing board/role/account/statistics data.

title: [EPIC] Reliable review fleet: account-aware capacity, adapter liveness, fallback and durable evidence
body:
## Outcome
A review either runs with correctly identified viable seats or returns a truthful, inspectable explanation. Missing health data cannot be called exhaustion; one exhausted account cannot disable healthy accounts; a failed attempt cannot disappear from the audit trail.

## Parent and specification
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/514
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-review-contracts.md#review-runtime

## Child work / delivery order
- [ ] P1 #472 — complete, fail-closed-for-exceptions capacity-check contract; paired with https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/705.
- [ ] P1 #479 — route/account-specific quota and fallback; do not combine unrelated accounts into a worst-case global block.
- [ ] P1 #460 — actionable auth/quota/billing/network/local-storage failure taxonomy and fallback.
- [ ] P1 #486 — reproduce worktree hangs, identify the real blocked process and prove cleanup; UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT remains a hypothesis until verified.
- [ ] DESIGN ONLY #476 — universal adapter architecture, not relocation of one model-specific constant.
- [ ] P1 #483 — OMP coverage in stalled-model reporting and diagnostic consistency.
- [ ] P2 #480 — durable compressed logs with verified migration and compatibility.
- [ ] P2 #469 — skipped-seat evidence before dispatch.
- [ ] P2 #468 — explicit cancellation/termination evidence where the process can record it.
- [ ] P2 #467 — preserve every stall/retry attempt.
- [ ] P2 #465 — trustworthy per-attempt account attribution; unknown rather than a guessed concurrent usage join.

## Explicit gate
#476 implementation remains blocked until the capacity crisis tracked by #472 and agent-tools#705 is resolved AND Alex explicitly approves implementation. This grooming and the accompanying documentation PR are NOT that approval. Existing narrow #474 wiring remains credited; no need to reimplement it.

## Dependencies and boundaries
Inventory/health comes from harness-cli's public contract, tracked in https://github.com/alex-mextner/harness-cli/issues/26; provider-specific probes must not be copied into review-cli. Review owns board composition, role-preserving fallback and review-call evidence. The entity UI is #487; spec-review UX is #484, not part of the runtime engine.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A nonempty, fully covered candidate set is required for all_exhausted=true; unknown, stale, malformed, unmapped and partially collected candidates make that assertion false.
- [ ] Authentication, billing, quota, transport, local storage and activity signals remain distinguishable; credentials are redacted.
- [ ] Healthy compatible candidates are tried before terminal failure; no endless retry loop or false successful review.
- [ ] Account and attempt IDs join dispatch, retries, skips, logs and terminal outcome without ambiguous time-only inference.
- [ ] Tests cover zero-output and after-first-output stalls, silent-but-progressing work, failed cleanup, zero seats, mixed accounts and interrupted migrations.
- [ ] A completion record links source revision, reproducible test/CI evidence and any separately performed live validation. Temporary screenshot paths are not durable proof.

## Non-goals
No automatic purchase, authentication, quota reset, destructive log cleanup or changes to protective merge rules. No universal default timeout is chosen by this grooming.

title: spec-web: persist document revisions and compare any two captured versions
body:
## What
Implement the document-history outcome from #484: persist bounded, content-identified spec revisions, expose read-only history/compare data and provide a usable version selector/diff view without changing the live document.

## Why (motivation)
#484 simultaneously describes versioning as not implemented and force-checks it using local /tmp screenshots. PR #485 is still open and its subject concerns other UX changes. An unverified screenshot is not proof of a durable history data model. Inspect and reuse any existing branch work before implementing; do not duplicate it.

## User impact
A reviewer can compare earlier drafts, including uncommitted edits and specs outside git, and keep the selected historical comparison stable while the live file changes.

## Cost of inaction
Only the current spec is inspectable and changes between edits cannot be reviewed reliably.

## Parent / specification
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/484
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-review-contracts.md#versioned-spec-review

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A documented schema/migration captures observed document content with stable revision IDs, content hashes and observation timestamps; mtime is a change hint, not the sole identity.
- [ ] Unchanged content is deduplicated; a restart, concurrent comment/reply write or failed write cannot corrupt existing comments or versions.
- [ ] Retention is bounded and explicitly defines behavior for versions referenced by anchor events; unavailable older content is reported rather than silently replaced.
- [ ] A read-only API lists/fetches captured versions and compares two chosen versions or a version with live content; it does not require a git repository or imply unobserved edits were captured.
- [ ] History UI labels revisions clearly and remains usable with SSE updates, empty history, long documents and narrow screens.
- [ ] Tests cover content changes with identical mtime, rapid changes, restart, retention and concurrent persistence. Browser interaction proof and durable screenshots reference the merged revision.

## Priority / dependencies
P2. This history model is a prerequisite for persisted anchor-change auditing. Existing partial branch work is baseline to assess, not completed acceptance.

title: spec-web: persist anchor-change events with old/new revision, position and diff
body:
## What
Persist the history of a comment's anchor as the spec changes. Retain old and new revision/position/text, resolution status and the reason/confidence for any proposed reanchor. Render an inspectable diff rather than only a current-render heuristic.

## Why (motivation)
The original request in #484 was to track what happened to an anchor. Its partial PR uses client-side word overlap against current content; the issue itself acknowledges that this is not a persisted audited event or full history. Re-rendering a suggestion does not satisfy that outcome.

## User impact
A reviewer can understand where a comment used to point and what changed, including after restart or several successive edits.

## Cost of inaction
An ambiguous fuzzy match can conceal drift and the original context disappears after later edits.

## Parent / specification / dependencies
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/484
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-review-contracts.md#versioned-spec-review
Depends on revision identity/history: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/493
Partial UX baseline: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/485

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Persist append-only anchor-change events referencing the comment and old/new captured revision, section/offset/text, observed timestamp and resolution method.
- [ ] Exact, suggested, ambiguous and unresolved states are distinct. A fuzzy candidate never silently becomes a confirmed anchor and does not overwrite original evidence.
- [ ] Duplicate quotes, renamed/moved headings, deletion and multiple successive changes remain inspectable without a false-positive relocation.
- [ ] Restart and concurrent comment/reply writes preserve the event chain; duplicate change processing is idempotent.
- [ ] UI shows old/new context and a text diff, retaining a clear unresolved fallback when no trustworthy successor exists.
- [ ] Integration tests and browser evidence demonstrate the multi-revision workflow; local /tmp image paths alone do not satisfy acceptance.

## Priority
P2. Reuse existing comment/reply persistence and partial UI work; do not create a second independent store.

title: Entities: join review configuration and live harness inventory in one truthful read model
body:
## What
Extend the shipped `review entities` Phase-0 model with the public harness inventory/health contract. Reuse board, role/model and call-stat data; do not add a competing provider/account discovery engine.

## Why (motivation)
#487 currently has a static report but its live enrichment remains unimplemented. The requested entity relationships cannot be reconstructed reliably by separate UI-specific scans or by merging all accounts sharing a model label.

## User impact
One view explains configured harness/provider/vendor/account/model/version/effort relationships and actual availability with source freshness and incomplete-coverage warnings.

## Cost of inaction
The future TUI repeats inconsistent one-shot reports and silently hides inaccessible accounts.

## Parent / specification / dependencies
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/487
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-review-contracts.md#entity-browser
Producer: https://github.com/alex-mextner/harness-cli/issues/26
Delivered baseline: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/488

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Text, JSON and interactive consumers share one versioned read model; existing Phase-0 fields/semantics have a documented compatibility path.
- [ ] Explicit live enrichment consumes the public harness contract and never imports provider-specific credential parsers.
- [ ] Stable account/route IDs join health and review statistics; unresolvable historical joins remain unknown rather than guessed from time/model.
- [ ] Missing binary, unsupported schema, partial collection and stale health are visible; none are rendered as healthy zero-usage accounts.
- [ ] Fixture tests cover all entity relationships, multiple accounts behind one provider, absent enrichment and equivalent totals across views.

## Priority
P2. The model contract can be tested against fixtures before live provider coverage is complete. No authentication, account rotation or billing mutation.

title: Entities: keyboard TUI with drill-down, refresh and non-TTY fallback
body:
## What
Build the terminal-native interactive surface requested by #487 over the shared entity read model, not another independent report. Provide list/detail/stats navigation, explicit refresh status and a dashboard link.

## Why (motivation)
Phase 0 is a one-shot text/JSON report; it is not the requested interactive TUI. The remaining interaction work needs a dependency decision and terminal acceptance rather than being implied by that report's merge.

## User impact
A user can navigate entity relationships and inspect health/statistics without manually correlating several CLI outputs.

## Cost of inaction
The headline feature remains unimplemented while the tracker may appear complete after only a flat report.

## Parent / specification / dependency
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/487
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-review-contracts.md#entity-browser
Depends on shared model: https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/issues/495

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Compare an optional terminal UI dependency with existing/minimal tooling, record the choice and preserve lightweight CLI/help imports.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, focus, filtering, drill-down and a usable small-terminal layout expose list, detail and statistics from the same model.
- [ ] Non-TTY and an explicit no-TUI option produce the existing readable report without control-sequence noise; JSON remains machine-readable.
- [ ] Refresh preserves selection by stable ID, shows stale/error status, avoids overlapping refresh work and exits cleanly on cancellation.
- [ ] A dashboard deep-link references the appropriate entity/context without introducing automatic account actions.
- [ ] PTY/interaction tests and durable terminal screenshots cover navigation, resize, missing live data, refresh and clean exit.

## Priority / scope
P2. Read-only first delivery. The optional account-rotation action mentioned in the original Phase 3 is not silently implemented or counted complete; it requires a separate explicitly approved, confirmation-gated change.
